case_title: Sardar Ali Khan v. State of Uttar Pradesh through Principal Secretary Home Department & Anr.
accused_victim_relationship: Acquaintance of the victim's late father; civil dispute (prior dispute) over the sale of the plot
mitigating_circumstances: Accused stated to be about 87 years old; complaint lodged about four years after the civil suit
trial_court_outcome: Discharge application rejected; Magistrate issued summoning order (later challenged under s.482 Cr.P.C.)
high_court_outcome: Section 482 Cr.P.C. application dismissed; order dated 12 March 2018 (Criminal Misc. Application No. 5684 of 2016)
neutral_facts: The accused states that they bought a plot of land from the victim under a sale deed executed in late December 1993 and registered in early January 1994. The victim died in December 1997, and his heir later obtained mutation of the inherited property in November 1998. In August 2008 the heir filed a civil suit seeking cancellation of the sale deed. The suit alleged that the deed was obtained falsely and fraudulently by the accused and the accused's brother, who made use of the victim's acquaintance. The civil suit did not allege impersonation or forgery of signatures. The accused had separately filed a civil suit against the heir seeking an injunction over constructions on the plot. In April 2012 the accused's brother lodged a complaint alleging that the heir had stolen the original sale deed from the mutation file. In September 2012 the heir lodged a criminal complaint against the accused and the brother alleging forgery and impersonation, about four years after the civil suit was filed. According to the accused, the heir also signed the sale deed as a witness. The material before the authorities consisted of the registered sale deed and the civil and criminal pleadings. A case was registered at the police station on the criminal complaint.
financial_property_loss: Not applicable (no money loss stated; plot No.102 is the disputed property)
motive: alleged: obtaining the sale deed of the plot by fraud, using the victim's acquaintance; not decided by the Court
key_evidence_accepted: No trial evidence assessed; Court relied on sale deed registration date (5 January 1994), civil suit filing (24 August 2008) and absence of forgery or impersonation allegations in the civil suit
trial_duration: offence: not given; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 12.03.2018; Supreme Court: January 24, 2020
legal_representation: Accused: Prashant Bhushan, Omanakuttan K.K., Cheryl D'Souza. Respondents: Ankit Goel, R.K. Gupta, Sudarshan Rajan, Mahesh Kumar, Md. Quamar Ali, Vijay Kumar Sharma (Sudarshan Rajan for the complainant); State counsel not separately identified
investigation_status: Private complaint lodged 20 September 2012 (Complaint Case No. 708 of 2012); case registered at Police Station Kaimganj; no charge sheet mentioned
appeal_history: Trial court (Magistrate): discharge rejected and summoning order issued; High Court: s.482 Cr.P.C. application dismissed on 12.03.2018; Supreme Court: appeal allowed and proceedings quashed
prosecution_argument: Complaint is not barred by limitation (contended by complainant's counsel)
defence_argument: Civil dispute over the sale deed is for the civil court; complaint is an abuse of process; complainant signed the sale deed as a witness; long delay in filing the complaint; accused is about 87 years old
legal_principle_applied: Where the same issue is pending before a civil court, criminal proceedings on it amount to abuse of process; quashing under s.482 Cr.P.C. where serious factual disputes of civil nature exist
other_sentence_order: Complaint Case No. 708 of 2012 quashed along with consequential Magistrate orders; civil court free to decide the pending suits on their merits
